durable_cleanup.requested_by: The user, choosing a Laravel-style jobs/failed_jobs design made atomic on every connection
durable_cleanup.design: features.extension_cleanup.jobs names a job connection with an outbox destination. Every configured database connection gets a jobs.PrepareOutboxIn producer for that destination and the outbox schema; deletions through a connection other than the extension store's enqueue foundry.extensions.cleanup (slots.CleanupRequest: owner name and persisted identity) inside the deletion transaction. The handler settles in a store transaction: it skips an owner that exists again, otherwise runs metadata/translations/attachments CleanupIdentity, which share the typed Cleanup logic. Invalid owners or identities fail permanently; other failures retry and surface in failed-job inspection. Only deletion observers receive the queue, so descriptors in job handlers never depend on the dispatcher.
durable_cleanup.validation: Build refuses the setting without features.extensions, features.outbox and an outbox destination for the connection; construction requires a durable job backend; startup compares current_database() and pg_postmaster_start_time() of every connection with the outbox connection's, answered by each pool's primary
tests: articles TestDurableCleanupAfterDeletionThroughAnotherPool: rolled-back deletion leaves no job; committed deletion leaves one outbox row and its data while no worker runs; a worker started afterwards removes metadata, translations and the logo
